newsitem.title: CHINA: China to restructure coal industry, boost exports.
newsitem.headline: China to restructure coal industry, boost exports.

text.p: China will restructure and streamline its coal industry this year, merging major companies into more efficient groups to boost exports by the world's largest coal producer, state media said on Sunday.

The restructuring is seen boosting exports to 40 million tonnes a year by the end of the century, up from 30 million tonnes in 1996, the China Daily Business Weekly said, quoting Wang Changchun, president of the China National Coal Import and Export Corp.
China's coal output was estimated at 1.35 billion tonnes in 1996, up 4.6 percent compared with the previous year, making it the world's biggest coal producer.

China would gather 14 state-owned coal firms into four groups to boost the competitiveness of an industry that was being forced to learn to compete in China's fledgling sink-or-swim market economy, the Business Weekly said.
The groups would be responsible for trade, use of coal, construction and equipment manufacturing, it said.

The first group, the China Coal Industry Import and Export Group, would be formed in April, merging four companies including the National Coal Import and Export Corp, it said. The group's annual turnover was expected to be 1.7 billion yuan ($205 million) in 1997, the newspaper said.

Schedules for forming the other three organisations -- the China Coal Comprehensive Utility Group, the China Coal Construction and Development Group and China Coal Materials and Equipment Group -- had yet to be completed, it said, quoting vice-minister for coal, Zhao Baoming.
China Mei Trust and Investment Co, a profitable state-owned shareholding enterprise set up in 1996, would be run independently, the newspaper said.

To boost exports, China would set up transport companies able to move 40 million tonnes of coal a year. Currently, mining and transport are supervised separately by the ministries of coal industry and railways, it said.
The umbrella groups formed after the restructuring would control shares of their subsidiaries and share in the profits, the newspaper said.

China's coal industry is chronically inefficient, and of China's 93 key state-owned coal mines, only 55 were profitable last year. That was still more than double the 26 that were profitable in 1995, officials have said.

China has said it would open at least 300 coal projects to foreign investors with priority to projects in pit-head power plants, coal transport facilities and coal-bed methane. It has not said whether investors could export output. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
